## What it is

- The **Les Paul** was "first sold by the Gibson Guitar Corporation in 1952" (Wikipedia, "Gibson Les Paul").
- Its **humbucker** pickups were designed by Seth Lover and "debuted on Les Pauls in 1957" (Wikipedia).
- Four knobs (two volume, two tone) and a three-way switch (Wikipedia). Each pickup has its own volume and tone.
- Scale 24.75 inches: a little shorter than a Fender (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- A **humbucker** is two coils side by side, wound and magnetised opposite ways. Hum makes opposite voltages in the two coils and cancels; the string's signal adds (Wikipedia, "Pickup (music technology)").
- Two coils are wider than one: they average the string over a longer stretch, which softens the high harmonics (Tillman, 2002).
- More wire means a lower resonance: humbuckers sound fuller and darker than single coils.
- In the middle position, turning **one** volume down changes the other pickup too: they share the output.

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="lespaul" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;rhythm&quot;}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Rhythm (neck).</b> Thick and warm.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="lespaul" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;treble&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Treble (bridge).</b> Brighter, with more bite. Turn the amp to <b>Crunch</b> or <b>Lead</b> and play it again.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="lespaul" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;both&quot;}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Both.</b> Fuller than each alone, a little hollow.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="lespaul" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;both&quot;,&quot;vol1&quot;:6}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Both, neck volume at 6.</b> The mix leans to the bridge pickup.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="lespaul" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;rhythm&quot;,&quot;tone1&quot;:0}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Neck, tone at 0.</b> Very dark: a "woman tone" kind of sound (the name is players' slang).</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="lespaul" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;both&quot;,&quot;phase&quot;:true}" data-play="chord"><p><b>What if: neck out of phase.</b> Not on a stock Les Paul. The two pickups now subtract: the low harmonics cancel, a thin, nasal sound.</p></div>
```

::: {.works-cited}
"Gibson Les Paul." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibson_Les_Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibson_Les_Paul). 1952; Seth Lover's humbuckers on Les Pauls from 1957; two volume, two tone, three-way; 24.75 in; Knopfler 1958 on Money for Nothing, Lukather 1959 in the Rosanna video.

Lemme, Helmuth E. W. "The Secrets of Electric Guitar Pickups." [buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/](https://buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/). Resonance of most pickups with a normal cable 2,000-5,000 Hz; inductance 1-10 H (not read directly: certificate expired 2026-11-26; unverified).

"Pickup (music technology)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)). Single coils pick up hum; humbucker coils cancel it; self-capacitance + cable resonate with the inductance; more turns, lower resonance.

Tillman, J. Donald. "Response Effects of Guitar Pickup Position and Width." 2000, updated 17 Oct. 2002. [www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html](https://www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html). Pickup point response sin(pi x F / (L F0)) = a comb filter; aperture term; Strat neck / middle / bridge 6.375 / 3.875 / 1.625 in, 1 in aperture; humbucker about 2.5 in; out-of-phase cancellation.
:::
